DI64 is a medical diagnosis code used in the Danish healthcare system to classify a stroke without specified information regarding whether it was caused by a hemorrhage or an infarction [^src1]. Within the context of the Danish Clinical Quality Program (RKKP) and its national databases, this code plays a critical role in tracking patient outcomes, specifically for individuals diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] [^src1]. 

The primary significance of DI64 lies in its application as a clinical quality indicator. It is utilized to measure the incidence of [[iskaemisk-apopleksi|Iskæmisk apopleksi]] among patients with atrial fibrillation, serving as a metric for inadequate anticoagulation therapy [^src3]. When calculating the incidence of ischemic stroke, DI64 is used alongside [[di63|DI63]] (cerebral infarction) and sometimes in combination with [[dz501|DZ501]] (contact for other physical therapy) paired with either DI63 or DI64 [^src1]. Data for these indicators is typically extracted from the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregisteret), capturing patient trajectories where DI63 or DI64 is recorded as the action diagnosis, or where DZ501 is the action diagnosis combined with DI63 or DI64 as a secondary diagnosis [^src2].
